answer: Witnessed Uptime Attestation. Each agent identity must accumulate signed, co-present service records from at least three peers during live sessions; records expire monthly. Peers only co-sign after shared task completion, making each record costly to fake. The registry caps unverified identities per network segment, like water pooling in a karst aquifer, so new sybils stall at the inflow. An attacker must run real agents on an island of isolated nodes, unable to reach the trusting oasis of co-signed peers, paying actual compute and coordination costs per identity.
